projects.title: RoomLight Data Spine
projects.tagline: A local-first environmental sensing spine that preserves sensor identity, calibration, uncertainty, human authority, and field receipts.
projects.story: RoomLight Data Spine connects identified room or field sensors to local packets, calibration and freshness checks, safety envelopes, human review, and evidence receipts. The retained source lineage includes starter firmware and the v0.2.2 safety patch. Publication Pack 1 makes the architecture and its boundaries inspectable while keeping live deployment, certified measurement, and actuator authority behind future physical receipts.
projects.summary: RoomLight observes stated conditions and preserves the context needed to inspect them. It separates readings from interpretation, interpretation from authority, and authority from equipment control. Stale, missing, disagreeing, uncalibrated, or implausible data should be quarantined rather than smoothed into false confidence.
projects.see: The local sensor-to-receipt architecture, calibration and packet-quality gates, safety envelope, human-review path, fixed-data Field Bench, retained starter-firmware lineage, and planned instrumented installation.
projects.proof: Seven public artifacts are connected: three reviewed SVG visuals, two public briefs, one fixed-data browser Field Bench, and the PAT Mk.1 Field integration. The Field Bench uses synthetic packets only, connects to no hardware, stores nothing, sends nothing, and controls nothing. Starter firmware and v0.2.2 safety lineage are retained as known source materials rather than mounted as fake downloads.
projects.next: Build an instrumented starter installation using named sensor models, stated calibration methods, visible local packet logs, packet-dropout and disagreement tests, manual interventions, maintenance records, and signed field receipts. Any actuator experiment must remain separately authorized, equipment-specific, bounded, fail-safe, and manually overridable.
projects.claimBoundary: RoomLight Data Spine is a local sensing and evidence architecture, not a certified instrument, medical device, emergency service, environmental safety guarantee, professional inspection, or automatic control authority. The published Field Bench uses fixed synthetic data and proves only presentation, packet review, quarantine logic, human disposition, and demonstration-receipt behavior. It does not prove live accuracy, code compliance, indoor-air safety, hazard detection, secure deployment, long-term reliability, or permission to control equipment.
